title: Gigantol ameliorates DSS-induced colitis via suppressing beta2 integrin mediated adhesion and chemotaxis of macrophage.
authors: Yu, Weilai; Li, Boyang; Chen, Luxi; Chen, Qiu; Song, QingQing; Jin, Xiaosheng; Yin, Yandan; Tong, Haibin; Xue, Liwei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药化合物gigantol通过抑制beta2整合素介导的巨噬细胞黏附与趋化改善结肠炎，属于蛋白-蛋白互作与炎症机制研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Dendrobium, recognized as "Shihu" in traditional Chinese medicine, holds a rich history of medicinal utilization documented in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. Ancient texts like "Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing" extol Dendrobium's virtues as a superior herbal medicine fortifying "Yin" and invigorating the five viscera. Dendrobium is extensively employed for the treatment of gastrointestinal inflammatory disorders, showcasing significant therapeutic efficacy, particularly against ulcerative colitis (UC), within the realm of Chinese ethnopharmacology. Dendrobium plays crucial pharmacological roles due to its rich content of polysaccharides, alkaloids, phenanthrenes, and bibenzyls. Gigantol, a prominent bibenzyl compound, stands out as one of the most vital active constituents within Dendrobium, the gigantol content of Dendrobium leaves can reach approximately 4.79 mug/g. Its significance lies in being recognized as a noteworthy anti-inflammatory compound derived from Dendrobium. AIM OF THE STUDY: Given the pivotal role of gigantol as a primary active substance in Dendrobium, the therapeutic potential of gigantol for gastrointestinal diseases remains enigmatic. Our present investigation aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effects of gigantol on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and reveal its potential mechanism in countering UC activity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The protective efficacy of gigantol against colitis was assessed by examining the histopathological changes and conducting biochemical analyses of colon from DSS-challenged mice. Assessments focused on gigantol's impact on improving the intestinal epithelial barrier and its anti-inflammatory effects in colonic tissues of colitis mice. Investigative techniques included the exploration of the macrophage inflammatory signaling pathway via qPCR and Western blot analyses. In vitro studies scrutinized macrophage adhesion, migration, and chemotaxis utilizing transwell and Zigmond chambers. Furthermore, F-actin and Rac1 activation assays detailed cellular cytoskeletal remodeling. The potential therapeutic target of gigantol was identified and validated through protein binding analysis, competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assay. The binding sites between gigantol and its target were predicted via molecular docking. RESULTS: Gigantol ameliorated symptoms of DSS-induced colitis, rectified damage to the intestinal barrier, and suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines in colonic tissues. Intriguingly, gigantol significantly curtailed NF-kappaB signaling activation in the colons of DSS-induced colitis mice. Notably, gigantol impaired the beta2 integrin-dependent adhesion and migratory capacity of RAW264.7 cells. Moreover, gigantol notably influenced the cytoskeleton remodeling of RAW264.7 cells by suppressing Vav1 phosphorylation and Rac1 activation. Mechanistically, gigantol interacted with beta2 integrin, subsequently diminishing binding affinity with intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1). CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, these findings elucidate that gigantol ameliorates DSS-induced colitis by antagonizing beta2 integrin-mediated macrophage adhesion, migration, and chemotaxis, thus it may impede macrophage recruitment and infiltration into colonic tissues. This study suggests that gigantol shows promise as a viable candidate for clinical colitis therapy.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：石斛（Dendrobium）在传统中医中被誉为“石斛”，在《中国药典》中有着丰富的药用历史记载。古代文献如《神农本草经》推崇石斛为一种上品草药，能滋养“阴”并强健五脏。石斛广泛用于治疗胃肠道炎症性疾病，在中国民族药理学领域显示出显著的疗效，尤其是对溃疡性结肠炎（UC）。石斛因其富含多糖、生物碱、菲类和联苄类化合物而发挥重要的药理作用。Gigantol，一种突出的联苄类化合物，是石斛中最重要的活性成分之一，石斛叶片中gigantol的含量可达约4.79微克/克。其重要性在于被公认为源自石斛的一种值得关注的抗炎化合物。研究目的：鉴于gigantol作为石斛中主要活性物质的关键作用，其对胃肠道疾病的治疗潜力仍属未知。本研究旨在评估gigantol对葡聚糖硫酸钠（DSS）诱导的结肠炎的治疗效果，并揭示其对抗UC活性的潜在机制。材料与方法：通过检查DSS诱导结肠炎小鼠的结肠组织病理学变化并进行生化分析，评估gigantol对结肠炎的保护功效。评估重点在于gigantol对改善肠上皮屏障的影响及其在结肠炎小鼠结肠组织中的抗炎作用。研究技术包括通过qPCR和Western blot分析探索巨噬细胞炎症信号通路。体外研究利用transwell和Zigmond小室检测巨噬细胞黏附、迁移和趋化性。此外，F-actin和Rac1激活实验详细描述了细胞骨架重塑。通过蛋白质结合分析、竞争性酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）和药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）分析，鉴定并验证了gigantol的潜在治疗靶点。通过分子对接预测了gigantol与其靶点之间的结合位点。结果：Gigantol改善了DSS诱导结肠炎的症状，修复了肠道屏障损伤，并抑制了结肠组织中促炎细胞因子的产生。有趣的是，gigantol显著抑制了DSS诱导结肠炎小鼠结肠中NF-kappaB信号的激活。值得注意的是，gigantol损害了RAW264.7细胞中β2整合素依赖性黏附和迁移能力。此外，gigantol通过抑制Vav1磷酸化和Rac1激活，显著影响RAW264.7细胞的细胞骨架重塑。机制上，gigantol与β2整合素相互作用，随后降低了与细胞间黏附分子-1（ICAM-1）的结合亲和力。结论：总之，这些发现阐明gigantol通过拮抗β2整合素介导的巨噬细胞黏附、迁移和趋化性来改善DSS诱导的结肠炎，从而可能阻碍巨噬细胞向结肠组织的募集和浸润。本研究提示gigantol有望成为临床结肠炎治疗的可行候选药物。
